context.guidance: Serialise only the fields a response needs, using explicit allow-lists or response shapes rather than whole models or nested records. Remove Personal Data Elements the requester is not entitled to see, so each response stays within the Purpose for which the data was collected under §6(1). Apply the same field limits on every route that returns the same record, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for access control.

value.fix: Stop returning whole model or record objects in responses. Define an explicit allow-list response shape (a DTO or serializer) for each endpoint that lists only the fields the requester is entitled to see, and serialize through it, for example `const { id, name, email } = record` or `toResponse(record)`, not `res.json(record)`. Remove any nested records or Personal Data Elements outside that list. Put the field allow-list in one shared serializer and use it on every route that returns the same record, so access limits match across all paths. Add a test for each route that asserts the response keys match the allow-list and that restricted fields such as the «SECRET» value are absent.
